title: Hierarchical health probes and autoscaler damping to stabilize SLOs during region failover
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During simulated and real multi-region failovers we've observed autoscaler thrashing and brief SLO violations caused by aggressive readiness/liveness probes and lack of damping on the scaling signal. This ticket standardizes a hierarchical probe strategy and implements autoscaler damping and circuit-breaker signals so that readiness transitions and scaling decisions preserve 99th-p latency and error budget targets during failover and burst events.

Goals:
- Prevent pod churn and scale flapping during region failovers and cold-start waves.
- Ensure failover does not cause sustained SLO violations (target: <2% error budget burn in a 1-hour window for critical routes).
- Provide deterministic failure modes: graceful load-shedding and conservative readiness to avoid routing traffic to partially-initialized instances.

High-level approach:
1) Hierarchical probes: fast liveness (process alive), conservative readiness (service-level checks + KV cache warm indicator + model weights loaded). Readiness requires both app readiness and a separate "model-warmed" gate for inference workers. Readiness transitions will be rate-limited with a 15s min stableWindow and jitter to avoid synchronized readiness storms across replicas.
2) Autoscaler damping: introduce smoothing of the scale metric (moving average over 30s to 2m depending on route) and a minimum stabilization window for scale-down (120s). For HPA/KEDA-backed policies, add an intermediate controller that translates circuit-breaker and probe signals into a throttled scale recommendation.
3) Circuit-breaker integration: expose circuit-breaker state (open/half-open/closed) as a metric with clear semantics. When the circuit is open for a model shard or region, scale decisions should favor maintaining capacity in fallback regions and prevent aggressive ramp-down.
4) Load-shedding priorities: implement a token-based admission control at the ingress layer for non-critical routes (batch, diagnostics). On overload/failover, non-SLA traffic is proactively rejected with TTL-coded error to preserve critical SLOs.
5) Multi-region failover playbook: update runbook to include staged readiness gating, scaling damping toggles, and verify rollback steps.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary in eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 failover test shows no more than 1.5% 1-hour error budget burn for critical routes (measured on route-level SLO dashboard).
- Autoscaler logs show reduced scale up/down oscillations (measured as 75% reduction in >2-scale events within 5 minutes during tests).
- Readiness probe causes zero traffic to pods without model cache warmed; manifests include readinessGate annotation and gating logic documented in Confluence.
- Circuit-breaker state surfaced in Grafana and used by autoscaler translation controller; alerting configured for >5m open-state on critical shards.
- Load-shedding policy implemented for non-critical ingress routes with documented HTTP response semantics (429 / X-RateLimit-Reason header).

Implementation notes:
- Probe design: we will split probes into a lightweight HTTP /healthz/liveness (200 if process responsive) and /healthz/readiness which runs non-blocking checks: readiness returns 200 only after model shard loaded, KV cache >= warmThreshold, and dependency pings succeed. Readiness returns 503 with structured JSON for debugging when failing.
- Probe timings: liveness initialDelaySeconds=10, periodSeconds=10, failureThreshold=3. Readiness initialDelaySeconds=15, periodSeconds=10, failureThreshold=3, plus readiness gating logic with a stableWindow of 15s (server-side).
- Autoscaler controller: implement an aggregator service (scale-orchestrator) that consumes Prometheus metrics (request rate, p99 latency, rb-error-rate, circuit-breaker state) and emits smoothed desiredReplicaCount to a safe HPA target. Use exponential backoff on scale-up above a region-specific throttle to avoid simultaneous large scale-ups across regions.
- Metrics: add metric names and labels: inference_ready{region, model, shard}, circuit_state{region, model, shard}, autoscaler_signal_smoothed{route}. Use these for SLO dashboards and alerts.
- Backwards compatible: default to existing HPA behavior until feature flag enabled per namespace.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Conservative readiness increases cold-start latency for single-replica services but reduces risk of misrouting. We mitigate by pre-warming model shards and allowing controlled burst capacity in Dedicated pools.
- Smoothing introduces lag in scaling up for short bursts; we offset with short-term burst quota in the routing layer to handle transient spikes without immediate scaling.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: merge readiness probe changes behind feature flags; add model-warm metric. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2578)
- Week 2: deploy scale-orchestrator in canary region and run synthetic failover tests. (Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/scale-orchestrator)
- Week 3: enable for non-critical services, monitor; run chaos runbook for controlled region failover.
- Week 4: enable for critical routes if canary passes, update runbooks and handover to SRE.

Testing plan:
- Automated e2e harness to simulate region outage with load generator (link to harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/failover-test-harness).
- Load tests with Gradual ramp and step tests (50% traffic cut to eu-west-1 then failover to us-east-1).
- Observability: extended retention for route-level traces and token-level cost/latency breakdown during tests.

Runbook changes required:
- Add procedure to toggle autoscaler damping and readiness gating via infra CLI.
- Add checklist for pre-warm commands and model-cache validation prior to planned failovers.

Notes on follow-ups and open questions:
- Decide final smoothing windows per SLA class (P0 routes vs P2).
- Determine whether to integrate smoothing into KEDA directly or keep an external translator. KEDA patch may be upstreamable.
- Finalize load-shedding semantics for edge clients that retry aggressively.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/RUNTIME/Hierarchical+Probes+and+Autoscaler+Damping
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2578
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/scale-orchestrator
- Failover harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/failover-test-harness
- Incident notes from 2026-01-12 failover: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INC/2026-01-12+multi-region+failover

Ready to review: engineering design, metric names, and runbook changes. Next milestone: cluster canary in eu-west-1 on 2026-03-15.
